rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying the subject studied by immunology.
rubric.description: Immunology is the study of immunity or the immune system.
rubric.how: Look for a clear reference to immunity or the immune system as the subject of study.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining the immune system’s protective role.
rubric.description: It concerns the body's defense against disease.
rubric.how: Look for a reference to protection or defense against disease.

modelAnswer: Immunology is the branch of biology that studies the immune system and immunity.
It deals with the body's defense against disease.

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying the biosphere as a part or zone of Earth.
rubric.description: The biosphere is the part or zone of Earth where life is found.
rubric.how: Look for an indication that it is a part, zone, or region of Earth.

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating that life or living organisms are present there.
rubric.description: It is the region where living organisms exist.
rubric.how: Look for a reference to life or living organisms.

modelAnswer: The biosphere is the part or zone of Earth where life exists.
It includes the regions inhabited by living organisms.

items.followUp: What is meant by drawing a conclusion in the biological method?

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that results are communicated or reported.
rubric.description: Reporting of result is the communication of the findings of an investigation.
rubric.how: Look for communicating, reporting, or presenting the findings.

rubric.why: Award one mark for giving an appropriate way or audience for reporting results.
rubric.description: Results may be published or presented so others can learn about them.
rubric.how: Look for publication, presentation, or communication to the scientific community.

modelAnswer: Reporting of result is the communication of the findings of an investigation.
The results may be published in scientific journals or presented to the scientific community.

items.followUp: Name one disease transmitted by each of these mosquitoes: Culex and Anopheles.

rubric.why: Award one mark for correctly associating Culex with a disease it transmits.
rubric.how: Look for filariasis or elephantiasis linked to Culex.

rubric.why: Award one mark for correctly associating Anopheles with malaria.
rubric.how: Look for malaria linked to Anopheles.

modelAnswer: Culex mosquitoes are well known for transmitting filariasis (elephantiasis).
Anopheles mosquitoes are well known for transmitting malaria.

items.followUp: State two characteristics used to classify organisms into kingdoms.

rubric.why: Award one mark for one valid basis of the Five Kingdom System.
rubric.description: One basis is cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction, or phylogenetic relationship.
rubric.how: Look for any one valid classification basis.

rubric.why: Award one mark for a second, distinct valid basis.
rubric.description: A second basis may be cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction, or phylogenetic relationship.
rubric.how: Look for two different valid bases in the answer.

modelAnswer: The Five Kingdom System is based on characteristics such as cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.
Any two of these are valid bases.

items.followUp: What happens to a virus outside a living host cell?

rubric.why: Award one mark for describing viruses as intermediate between living and non-living.
rubric.description: Viruses are considered to lie at the boundary between living and non-living things.
rubric.how: Look for an explicit living/non-living boundary or borderline status.

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating how viral status depends on being inside or outside a host.
rubric.description: They show living characteristics inside a host but are inactive outside one.
rubric.how: Look for the contrast between the virus inside a host and outside it.

modelAnswer: Viruses are regarded as being on the boundary between living and non-living things.
They reproduce inside a living host cell but remain inactive outside a host.

items.followUp: What is meant by selective permeability of a cell membrane?

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating that the membrane allows some substances through.
rubric.description: The plasma membrane allows certain substances to pass through it.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that some substances are allowed to pass.

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating that it restricts other substances.
rubric.description: It prevents other substances from passing freely.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that passage is restricted or selective.

modelAnswer: The plasma membrane is called semi-permeable because it allows certain substances to pass through it.
It restricts the passage of other substances.

items.followUp: State one role of lysosomes in a cell.

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying digestion as a lysosome function.
rubric.description: Lysosomes carry out intracellular digestion, including digestion of food or foreign particles.
rubric.how: Look for intracellular digestion or digestion of material within the cell.

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying breakdown of worn-out cell parts or autolysis.
rubric.description: They can break down worn-out organelles and may cause autolysis.
rubric.how: Look for breakdown of worn-out or damaged organelles, or self-digestion.

modelAnswer: Lysosomes carry out intracellular digestion, breaking down food particles and foreign material.
They can also digest worn-out organelles and may cause autolysis of the cell.
